# EC 2.7.1.1 in Homo sapiens

What are the measured constants, and where did each come from?

## Parameters

| parameter | value | origin | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| km | 6 mM | literature | BRENDA ref 641068 |
| s0 | 10 mM | **yours** | chosen for this run |
| vmax | 0.25 mM/s | **yours** | chosen for this run |

A value marked **yours** describes the experiment, not the enzyme. No database reports it, and Caterva has not checked it.

## Conditions the values were measured under

Kinetic values move with pH, temperature and buffer. Two values measured under different conditions describe experiments nobody ran together.

- **km** — measured at pH 7.5, 30 °C

## The literature disagrees about km

The evidence ranked 3 values of km equal: 6 to 18. Running the model at each -- and at no other value, since no other value was measured -- the substrate remaining at t=10 ranges from 8.485 to 9.133. A factor of 1.08. This is the disagreement among the sources carried through the model. It is NOT an uncertainty estimate: the spread is bounded by which papers happen to be in BRENDA, not by any statement about the true value.

| value | result |
|---|---|
| 18 | 9.13281 |
| 6 (returned) | 8.48542 |
| 6.3 | 8.51371 |

## What Caterva would not do

These are not omissions. Each one is a decision, with the reason and what would change it.

- no band was produced across the 3 values the literature reports for km: no seed was supplied, and an ensemble nobody can reproduce is not evidence. Re-run with --seed N.

## Result

| time | [S] | [P] |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 10 | 0 |
| 10 | 8.48542 | 1.51458 |

51 time points; first and last shown. The full trajectory is in the CSV export.
